items.title: La-Z-Boy Swings to First-Quarter Loss From Declining Sales
items.summary: The furniture maker’s sales slid 3% to $475.7 million, missing analyst forecasts for a gain to $501 million.

items.title: Toll Brothers Records Lower Sales as Home Deliveries Decline
items.summary: The company’s home sales declined to $2.65 billion as it delivered 2,662 homes in the quarter, down from 2,959 a year ago.

items.title: What Does The S&P 500 Earnings Boom Say About The Stock Market?
items.summary: S&P 500 earnings per share are on pace to climb more than 50% in the second quarter.  Combining reported and yet-to-be-reported results, S&P 500 earnings are up 50.4%, according to the most recent data from FactSet.  Profit growth is broad, too, with 10 of the 11 S&P 500 sectors posting year-over-year earnings growth.

items.title: Why this popular Treasury-bond ETF is trading at its lowest since 2004
items.summary: One of the most heavily-traded ETFs tracking performance in the U.S. Treasury market has just fallen to its lowest level in over 20 years.

items.title: FactSet’s Kashner: Active Investors Prefer Performance to Cost
items.summary: As the ETF fee war kicks up again in new categories, cost still wins with vanilla investors. However, in active categories, FactSet’s Elisabeth Kashner breaks down a growing preference for performance in this midyear ETF flow look back.

items.title: Why Soaring Profit Margins Might Not Be So Sweet
items.summary: Some companies deserve the praise and attention that investors are giving them. Ones whose growing margins come from cutting their labor force don’t, Amir Goren writes.
